plugin_security.title: Advanced security
plugin_security.description: Two-factor authentication (TOTP), enforcement policy and login IP allow/deny lists

required.title: Two-factor authentication is required
required.grace: Finish setting it up before {{time}}, otherwise you will not be able to sign in.
required.desc: Please finish setting it up as soon as possible.

twofa.title: Two-factor authentication (TOTP)
twofa.desc: After you bind an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, ...), signing in also requires a 6-digit code.
twofa.noQr: In your authenticator app choose "enter a setup key manually" and use the key below (or the otpauth link). This build does not render a QR code.
twofa.cannotDisable: Your administrator requires two-factor authentication, so you cannot turn it off.

recovery.title: Save your recovery codes
recovery.once: Each code works once and is shown only now. Use one to sign in if you lose your phone.

policy.title: Enforcement policy
policy.desc: Decide who must enable two-factor authentication.

modeDesc.roles: Only users with the selected roles must enable it.

policy.rolesHint: Separate multiple roles with commas. Use role codes, not display names.
policy.graceHint: Users who have not bound yet can still sign in during the grace period and set it up on this page. After it ends they cannot sign in (super admins excepted); an administrator can reset them under User status. Changing the policy restarts the grace period.

users.resetConfirm: Reset two-factor authentication for {{name}}? Their key and recovery codes will be removed.

ip.hint: Deny rules win. When any enabled allow rule exists, only listed IPs may sign in. Saving checks that your own IP is not locked out.
